sections.h2: Where is the McMinn County Register of Deeds, and what does the office do?
sections.html:
Find the office on the main floor of the McMinn courthouse, 6 East Madison Avenue, Athens, TN 37303, or call (423) 745-1232. Cheryl Ingram is the elected Register. Counter service runs from half past eight in the morning until four in the afternoon.

Staff record conveyances, deeds of trust, leases and similar instruments, and they certify copies of anything on file. Voters choose the register countywide every four years. A seller here does not usually visit in person: the deed that transfers your house to a buyer usually arrives from the closing agent.

According to the county's register page, the counter takes debit and credit cards, with American Express excluded. That page prints no fee schedule, so ask the staff for a total when your deed runs long.

sections.h2: What is McMinn County like to sell in?
sections.html:
The legislature carved McMinn out in 1819 and named it for Joseph McMinn, a former governor. Athens serves as seat of government and is the biggest city. Etowah, Niota and Sweetwater are cities too, while Calhoun and Englewood are towns. Ridge and Valley terrain covers most of the county, and the Hiwassee River forms its southwestern edge against Bradley County.

Census QuickFacts lists 57,404 residents as of July 2025, a 7.8% gain over the April 2020 base. There are 24,424 housing units across 430 square miles of land, about 124 residents per square mile. Households earn a median $61,470, and renters pay a median $803 in gross rent.

  • Typical home value among owners, 2020 to 2024: $211,800.
  • Owner-occupancy rate: 75.8%.
  • People aged 65 and over: 21.1%.
  • Building permits in 2025: 125.

Three school systems serve the county. McMinn County Schools operates both high schools, with Athens City Schools and the Etowah School District teaching grades K through 8 inside their boundaries. Tennessee Wesleyan University sits in Athens.

sections.h2: What does recording a McMinn County deed cost in state tax?
sections.html:
Two state taxes apply at recording. The transfer tax is 37 cents for each $100 of the sale price or property value, whichever is higher. The mortgage tax is 11.5 cents for each $100 borrowed, and the first $2,000 of any debt is left out. Under the state's recordation tax manual the register collects both on the spot, and the grantee shown on the deed carries the transfer tax.

Tennessee recordation tax rates collected at the McMinn County register
TaxRateWho pays by default
Realty transfer tax$0.37 per $100 of price or valueGrantee (buyer)
Mortgage (indebtedness) tax$0.115 per $100, first $2,000 exemptBorrower
Receipt fee for the taxUp to $1 per receiptFiler

Source: Tennessee Department of Revenue rate page and recordation tax manual. A purchase contract can reassign these costs, so read yours before closing.

Try the county's Census median as a test case. A $211,800 sale is 2,118 hundreds, and 2,118 times $0.37 comes to $783.66 in transfer tax. A buyer financing $170,000 would owe mortgage tax on $168,000, or 1,680 hundreds at $0.115, which is $193.20.

sections.h2: What does the McMinn County register require before a deed is recorded?
sections.html:
McMinn County posts a checklist called Requirements to Record Documents. Any deed lacking one of its items risks rejection, so walk through it with whoever prepares your closing papers.

  • Preparer's name and address, matching the return envelope if you enclose one.
  • Grantee's address, along with the address for future tax bills.
  • Map and parcel number, legal description, and last book and page of title.
  • Each signature notarized, with the acknowledgment naming the signers and carrying the notary's seal and date.
  • A sworn oath of consideration giving whichever is larger, the price or the property's value.
  • For any document tied to debt, the sentence "Maximum principal indebtedness for TN tax recording purposes is $___."

A corrected document needs fresh signatures and acknowledgments, or a scrivener's affidavit stapled to it. The checklist also says documents sent without a stamped, self-addressed return envelope may be destroyed 90 days after recording, so include one if you want the original back.

sections.h2: Which McMinn County transfers owe no realty transfer tax?
sections.html:
Some transfers escape the $0.37 tax under the state manual, and a few matter in family and estate sales. Exempt transfers need no oath.

  • Transfers of a leasehold estate.
  • One spouse deeding to the other as a tenancy by the entirety begins or ends.
  • A deed signed by an executor to carry out a gift in a will.
  • Domestic decrees and deeds that adjust property rights between divorcing spouses.
  • Moves into or back out of a revocable living trust made by that owner or the owner's spouse.
  • Conveyances to or from a government body.

A quitclaim deed is taxed on the consideration given, yet the state taxes fair market value when its wording shows an intent to pass the property itself, such as "in fee simple." State revenue staff sometimes pull deeds from a random county and date range, set the sworn value beside the assessor's figure, and mail an inquiry letter if the two are far apart. An unusually low stated price on a McMinn County deed can draw that letter.

sections.h2: How do you search records or e-record documents in McMinn County?
sections.html:
The register accepts electronic recordings through Simplifile, Corporation Service Company (CSC) and eRecording Partners Network (EPN). Your title company will pick one of these routes at closing.

For searching, the county points researchers to US Title Search Network, which charges per search or a monthly fee. If that service gives you trouble, the register's page lists Progress Inc. at 1 (800) 394-7477. Assessor data is separate: the county's Assessor of Property, Keith Price, at (423) 745-2743, keeps parcel maps and property cards, and the state's assessment website lets you look up map and parcel numbers that every conveyance needs.

If you inherited a McMinn County house and need to sell, ask the register how the executor's deed should be worded, and ask the probate clerk for proof of authority.

sections.h2: Who bills the property tax when a McMinn County house sells?
sections.html:
County property tax goes to the McMinn County Trustee in the courthouse at 6 East Madison Avenue, phone (423) 745-1291. The current year's bill can be paid between October 1 and the end of February. Weekday hours are 8 to 4, and the office also opens on Saturday mornings in February.

The Trustee also handles applications for the state's Tax Relief Program, which helps elderly and disabled homeowners and disabled veterans. The county page sets the application cutoff at 35 days after the February 28 payment deadline. Relief repays part of a bill the owner has paid, so the bill itself still arrives.

Settlement of the current year's tax is a closing-table decision, so raise it with the closing agent early and get a payoff from the Trustee beforehand. If the owner name or mailing address on the roll is wrong, the assessor can fix it.

faqs.q: Where is a McMinn County deed recorded?
faqs.a: The McMinn County Register of Deeds does, in the Athens courthouse at 6 East Madison Avenue. Call (423) 745-1232 with questions. Title companies normally submit deeds electronically.

faqs.q: How much transfer tax applies when a McMinn County house sells?
faqs.a: Thirty-seven cents per $100 of the larger of price or value. At the county's $211,800 Census median that comes to $783.66, owed by the grantee unless the contract shifts it.

faqs.q: Can a deed be e-recorded in McMinn County?
faqs.a: Yes. The register takes e-recordings from Simplifile, CSC and eRecording Partners Network. Individuals without an account usually rely on a title company or attorney.

faqs.q: Is transfer tax owed on a sale of an inherited McMinn County house?
faqs.a: A deed an executor signs to carry out a gift in a will is exempt. The later sale to a buyer is taxed at the normal rate, so ask the register how each deed in the chain is treated.

faqs.q: Where is McMinn County property tax paid ahead of a closing?
faqs.a: Pay the McMinn County Trustee at the courthouse in Athens and call (423) 745-1291 for a payoff figure. Current-year bills are payable October 1 through the end of February.
